row1.text: Inventory — simplified, one picture per question

brief.text:
WHAT CHANGED, AND WHY IT IS SIMPLER

The first pass added instruments to the existing screen. This one takes things away until what is left reads at a glance.

ONE QUESTION PER TILE. Four tiles, each with one figure and one picture: what the shelf is worth (and its 30-day line), how healthy it is (one bar, coloured by state), what runs out inside your cover (crimson), and what has stopped moving (hatched amber). Nothing else stands between the page name and the list.

ONE ROW OF TOOLS. Search, a five-way state filter, category, sort. The filter's dots are the same colours as the health bar above it, so the tile and the filter are one idea.

ONE TABLE, ONE OPEN LINE. Five columns, generous rows, and a cover bar on every row so the eye finds the short bar before it reads a figure. Pressing a row opens it on the right — the big figure is how many days until it is empty, then the floor bar, four figures, thirty days of sales, and three actions.

GONE: the five-tile strip, the repair banner, the scatter map, the three lanes, the register's five extra columns, the rail of side panels, and three of the six artboards. What they said is either in a tile now or one press away in the open line.

Colour still answers one question each: crimson = running out, amber = caution and dead money, verdigris = healthy, oxide = the one thing to do next. Every value is the app's own tokens, type and components.
